summary: The firm represents Marrowind Packaging Corp. (Seller) in selling its corrugated packaging business to Tessaly Holdings LLC (Buyer) for $18,400,000 under a New York-law asset purchase agreement. The folder holds four documents: the APA, a Transition Services Agreement, a Bill of Sale and an Escrow Agreement. Three issues are planted. In the APA, a carve-out removes the indemnity cap from all of Seller's representation-breach claims. The TSA selects Delaware law and Delaware courts. The Bill of Sale defines 'Purchased Assets' without excluding the Excluded Assets. The APA's precedence clause lets each Ancillary Agreement control as to its own subject matter, so the APA does not cure the TSA or Bill of Sale problems. The Escrow Agreement is a clean distractor.

facts.value: Laws of the State of New York
State and federal courts located in New York County, New York
APA controls over Ancillary Agreements, except each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter
All assets used or held for use in the Business, other than the Excluded Assets
Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility, and the HOLLIS trademark

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Section 9.4(a) caps Seller's indemnity at 10% of the Purchase Price. Section 9.4(c) then states that the cap shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a). Section 9.2(a) covers breach of any Seller representation, not only fundamental representations, so the carve-out removes the cap for essentially every indemnity claim. Seller is left with liability up to and beyond the full Purchase Price, well above the $1,840,000 escrow.
detect_terms: shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a)
issues.expected_finding: The Section 9.4(c) carve-out leaves the 10% cap unable to bind any representation-breach claim, exposing Seller to uncapped liability. It should be narrowed to fundamental representations and fraud, with those claims capped at the Purchase Price.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: The TSA is governed by Delaware law and submits disputes exclusively to Delaware courts. The APA chooses New York law and New York County courts. Section 10.12 of the APA lets each Ancillary Agreement control as to its own subject matter, so the TSA clause is not overridden. Related disputes, such as set-off of TSA fees against indemnity claims, could therefore be split across two forums under two bodies of law.
detect_terms: laws of the State of Delaware
courts of the State of Delaware
issues.expected_finding: The TSA's Delaware law and forum clause conflicts with the APA's New York choice and is not cured by the precedence clause. It should be conformed to New York law and New York County courts.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: The Bill of Sale defines 'Purchased Assets' as all assets used or held for use in the Business. It does not carve out the Excluded Assets (cash, the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark), and it does not cross-refer to the APA definition. The Bill of Sale is the conveyancing instrument and controls as to its subject matter under APA Section 10.12, so it purports to transfer assets Seller agreed to retain.
detect_terms: used or held for use in the Business
issues.expected_finding: The Bill of Sale's broader 'Purchased Assets' definition could convey the Excluded Assets to Buyer. It should be revised to adopt the APA definition and expressly exclude the Excluded Assets.
